metadata.title: Honest Shortlist: Final Project Pitch
metadata.persona: none: Prathamesh's own first-person script, synthetic voice, disclosed in B00
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: Student pitch film: the brief says to narrate as yourself and not to use the instructor's name, persona or credit line, so every house bookend is dropped (hesitant writer, terms card, Claude composer, @NikBearBrown outro). B00 is a plain title with the synthetic-voice disclosure; B14 is a short close.

beats.narration_text: A network engineering posting lists skills, city, sometimes pay. On sponsorship, it often says nothing. For the fictional F one student I'm designing for, that silence is the problem.

beats.narration_text: Honest Shortlist will be a Python and Claude agent that watches public job boards and gives that student a short daily list of new postings, shipped as a GitHub repo with tests, a held-out evaluation, and a ten-document packet.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

shot.visual_intent: Three board stacks on the left; postings slide through a narrow gate into a short-list tray; the tray sits inside an open box tagged 'GitHub repo' with a test page, an eval sheet and a ten-page stack.
shot.motion_claim: Three board stacks on the left; postings slide through a narrow gate into a short-list tray; the tray sits inside an open box tagged 'GitHub repo' with a test page, an eval sheet and a ten-page stack.

beats.narration_text: Each claim, new, location, sponsorship, pay, will be labeled supported, contradicted, or insufficient against the posting's own text. Liveness will be checked by fetching the board again.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

shot.motion_claim: One shortlist card with four claim rows; a stamp lands on each row (check, cross, dash); a refresh arrow loops from the card back to a board stack.

beats.narration_text: Why care? It will show its evidence and say the posting doesn't say, instead of guessing. I haven't examined alternatives yet. In my first job-search assignment, I will compare LinkedIn job alerts and a chat assistant.

beats.narration_text: A hiring manager or engineer screening for that role will read the read-me and sample output, then run one command, all within a minute. Each claim will link to its posting text, beside an evaluation table that shows the failures.

beats.narration_text: It will show I can build prompt contracts, with a validator that rejects anything off-schema; an agent loop with budgets, exits, and a stop the model doesn't control; and permissions enforced in code, with boundary tests.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

shot.motion_claim: Three blocks rise in a row, each with a small evidence page: contract (a schema slot rejecting a bent card), loop (a ring with an exit gate), permissions (a fence with an allow-list tag).

beats.narration_text: Then source grounding with an M C P style tool, verification and versioned memory, a held-out evaluation with five or more deliberate failures, and a human approval gate bound to the exact shortlist.

beats.narration_text: Out, by design: no LinkedIn or Indeed scraping, only public Greenhouse, Lever, and Ashby data. And it will never apply, email, message, or log in.

beats.narration_text: First, a one-board watch. Run one will set a baseline. Run two will report only new postings, on a real second day, or from a saved earlier response, clearly labeled. Anyone will be able to check the raw responses and the diff.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: The risk: keywords mislead. Visa can be the payments company; authorized to work, without the word sponsorship, answers neither question. So insufficient will be the default, and public H one B employer data will stay a separate company signal, never a claim about the posting.

qc.sparse_reason: show-tell style: one drawn object or scene on a cream stage per beat, minimal labels, the voice carries the explanation. Only underfill and clustered are waived; edge-bleed, empty-frame and contrast still apply.

beats.narration_text: Writing Python myself, agent loops, policies in code, and evaluations that can say no are new to me. I already ran the Brutalist toolkit on Windows, diagnosed its failures, and reviewed and approved Claude's fixes. On my Reallocation recipe, I chose the persona, rules, and dates, while Claude drafted the code.
